input: word1 and word2 are ASCII lowercase strings of lengths n,m; empty strings accepted. n+m+2 fits the collection-size bound. Collections are ordinary finite dense arrays/lists, not subclasses, proxies, sparse/accessor-backed collections. Strings are ordinary/primitive strings. Every collection length and computed allocation size fits [0,4294967295], with padded sizes explicitly included. No concurrent mutation or built-in monkey-patching is allowed. Preconditions are not runtime-checked, and allocation/resource capacity or completion is not guaranteed by declared bounds. Python integer inputs are plain int, excluding bool.
return: Lexicographically greatest interleaving formed by repeatedly taking the first remaining character of either word, preserving each word order and using every character.
mutation_aliasing: Inputs and caller-held aliases remain unchanged; working state is private. The Solution instance retains no state. Result is an immutable string; no input strings are changed.
numeric: ASCII lexical comparison is identical across languages. Comparing complete remaining suffixes resolves equal current letters correctly; when suffixes are identical either choice is valid. Indices/counts are exact. All integer inputs/intermediates remain within [-9007199254740991,9007199254740991]; no bitwise coercion is used.
complexity: O((n+m)^2+1) worst-case time, explicitly counting repeated suffix slicing/comparison. O(n+m+1) live auxiliary/output space includes temporary suffixes, output chunks and final join. No linear-time claim is made. Bounds include ordinary built-in operations/allocations and assume bounded-word arithmetic, constant-time indexing, amortized append/pop and any explicitly stated hash/sort behavior.
